runs.notes: file-level green = every executed test in the file passed and nothing errored outside a test. ahead-of-reference = every failure in the file is a stale bun `test.failing` marker that now passes, i.e. mbun is MORE correct than bun there; it is NOT counted as green because the file still does not pass bun's suite as written.

REGRESSION_AGAINST_PREVIOUS_FULL_RUN.compared_to: target/integration/r5-bun (green 884, the most recent full run with per-file rows; the previously published 885 was a round-7/8 snapshot whose per-file data is gone)
REGRESSION_AGAINST_PREVIOUS_FULL_RUN.how_much_is_a_measurement_artefact: Little of it. Sampling 10 of the 43: one (assert/deep-equal.test.ts) has 22 of 22 failures be 'expected to fail but passed' and is genuinely ahead-of-reference; the other 9 are real failures of 1-2 assertions each. So node-side progress across rounds 6-10 did cost bun files, and this is a trade to be decided rather than absorbed.
REGRESSION_AGAINST_PREVIOUS_FULL_RUN.crash_bucket: 13 -> 0, which is real progress and unrelated to the green loss

baseline_for_comparison.binary: round-8 HEAD (23217dd), measured with the SAME corrected runner

runs.notes: A file that skipped itself (common.skip() -> '1..0 # Skipped:', exit 0) is classified `skipped`, never `pass`. common.mustCall is enforced from this binary onward (node registers its verifier in process.on('exit'), which previously never fired). Both corrections lower the number relative to previously published figures; the 44.5% published against round 8 was a product of both defects and was never real. Full estimate-vs-actual and methodology: compat/data/round-estimates.json and compat/README.md. A third verification defect was fixed after the previous entry: assert.throws ignored its error argument, so any throw satisfied any matcher. That removed 126 passes (25 of 25 sampled confirmed vacuous), which is why this figure is LOWER than the previously recorded 47.9%/54.7%.
runs.jobs_note: Measured at --jobs 6, not 8/10. Higher parallelism does not change the total (a jobs-6 full run moved exactly the 11 files the wave's agents claimed and no others) but it makes per-file attribution unreliable: individual pass->fail results at --jobs 10 have repeatedly failed to reproduce standalone. See compat/README.md 'A parallel guard invents regressions'.
runs.measurement_caveat: Measured on the build output directly. A binary COPIED to a different basename (mbun-<sha>) reports 10 phantom regressions across child_process/process/signal/module -- tests that re-spawn the runtime fail with 'spawn mbun ENOENT'. Snapshot to <dir>/bin/mbun instead; verified both ways.
runs.wave56_note: +174 gained, -11 REGRESSED, net +163 against the previous authoritative run. The 11 are REAL -- each reproduces 3/3 standalone, not a parallel-guard artefact -- and are the price of this round's runtime-wide changes (the process.nextTick queue split and entry-point error routing). Four are stack-overflow / uncaught-exception / mock-timer files that now time out; the rest are web-locks (2), crypto-worker-thread, permission-fs-require, repl-tab-complete-nested-repls and worker-process-env. Publishing the gross gain alone would misrepresent the round.
